limitations: General ANN models for sound level/acoustic comfort are less feasible due to complex physical and social environments (p. 177, 193).
Individual ANN models for sound level/acoustic comfort have limited application range (p. 177, 193).
Accuracy and reliability of group models depend on the specificity of the situation they are trained on (p. 177).
Subjective evaluations are varied between individual users and cannot be completely represented by computer models (p. 192, 207).
Field studies in this research were not controlled to meet research purpose, suggesting potential for further improvements with controlled studies (p. 192, 207).
Some inputs (e.g., subjective evaluations of physical conditions) cannot be gained at the design stage because these conditions or social users do not exist yet (p. 192).
Due to software limitations, only loudness and sharpness were studied as psychoacoustic parameters; other parameters like roughness were not included (p. 225).
The number of samples used in the lab models was limited, which might cause unreliable learning (p. 196, 213).
NeuroSolutions models require a larger sample size for training compared to Qnet (p. 185, 186, 194).
The prediction performance of ANN models (test coefficients) is generally not very high (all less than 0.8) (p. 207).

The models developed for predicting single sounds did not use 'sound category' as an input variable, which was found to be significantly related to subjective evaluations of sound preference for combined sounds (p. 218-219).
minimum_safe_summary: This PhD thesis investigates soundscape evaluation and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) modeling in urban open spaces, drawing on environmental psychology. It uses data from 19 field study sites in Europe and China, complemented by laboratory experiments, to analyze factors influencing subjective evaluations of sound level, acoustic comfort, and sound preference. Key findings indicate that natural sounds are preferred over mechanical sounds, and aural-visual interactions positively influence sound preference. Psychoacoustic parameters like loudness and sharpness are crucial for predicting sound preference. ANN models were developed to predict these subjective evaluations, with individual and group models generally outperforming general models, and acoustic comfort models showing better performance than sound level models. However, the models' overall prediction accuracy is noted as a limitation, along with the need for more controlled field studies and the inclusion of additional psychoacoustic parameters in future work.
